Dr Reed.zh: Reed 博士 · 设计学院

episodes.title: Home Again
episodes.scene_zh: 你从爱丁堡回到伦敦。Emma 和 Tom 在国王十字车站等你。

lines.en: Lin! Over here! Look at you. You look as if you've been away for a year, not a fortnight.
lines.zh: 林！这儿！看看你，像是走了一年，而不是两个星期。

lines.en: It feels like a year. So much happened that I've completely lost track of the days.
lines.zh: 感觉就像一年。发生了太多事，我完全记不清过了几天。

lines.en: We've been following everything online. Your dinners were all over the papers.
lines.zh: 我们一直在网上关注。你们的晚餐上了各大报纸。

lines.en: Only after the storm. Before that, nobody had heard of us.
lines.zh: 那是暴雨之后的事。在那之前，根本没人听说过我们。

lines.en: And? Did Jake really offer you a job in New York?
lines.zh: 然后呢？Jake 真的给了你纽约的工作？

lines.en: He did. I turned it down, at least for now.
lines.zh: 是的。我拒绝了，至少暂时拒绝了。

lines.en: You turned down New York? For Camden? I need to sit down.
lines.zh: 你拒绝了纽约？为了卡姆登？我得坐下缓缓。

lines.en: It isn't just Camden. I've decided to apply for a part-time master's in design here in London.
lines.zh: 不只是为了卡姆登。我决定在伦敦申请一个在职的设计硕士。

lines.en: That's brilliant! Is there anything you need first?
lines.zh: 太棒了！你需要先准备什么吗？

lines.en: An English test. They want an overall score of seven before the course starts in January.
lines.zh: 一个英语考试。一月开课前，他们要求总分 7 分。

lines.en: Seven out of what? Ten?
lines.zh: 满分多少？十分？

lines.en: Out of nine, Tom. Don't worry, Lin. Your English is miles better than when you first arrived.
lines.zh: 满分九分，Tom。别担心，林。你的英语比刚来时好太多了。

lines.en: Thanks. But chatting with friends is one thing. Doing it under exam conditions is quite another.
lines.zh: 谢谢。不过跟朋友聊天是一回事，在考试条件下说又是另一回事。

choice.q_zh: Tom 不敢相信你放弃了纽约，你说：

lines.en: Don't be so dramatic, Tom. Camden has better tea.
lines.zh: 别这么夸张，Tom。卡姆登的茶更好喝。

lines.en: She's got a point. American tea is a crime.
lines.zh: 她说得对。美国的茶简直是犯罪。

lines.en: New York can wait. I've got unfinished business here.
lines.zh: 纽约可以等。我在这儿还有事没做完。

lines.en: Unfinished business? That sounds very mysterious.
lines.zh: 没做完的事？听起来很神秘啊。

lines.en: Before we go, I made you something. Well, I bought it, but I chose the words.
lines.zh: 走之前，我给你做了个东西。好吧，是买的，但字是我挑的。

lines.en: A cake! It says "Not bad."
lines.zh: 蛋糕！上面写着“还不赖”。

lines.en: In Manchester, that's the highest compliment there is.
lines.zh: 在曼彻斯特，这可是最高评价。

lines.en: He spent twenty minutes arguing with the baker about the spelling.
lines.zh: 他为了拼写跟面包师吵了二十分钟。

lines.en: It's perfect. Honestly, really good. Not just not bad.
lines.zh: 太完美了。说真的，是真好，不只是还不赖。

quiz.q: 林回到伦敦后打算做什么？
options: 申请伦敦的在职设计硕士

quiz.q: 入学要求英语考试总分多少？
“quite another” 那句是什么意思？
options: 在考试条件下说英语完全是另一回事

episodes.next_zh: Emma 说她认识一个能帮你练口语的人——就在蓝门咖啡馆。

episodes.title: Arthur's Secret
episodes.scene_zh: Emma 说的那个能帮你练口语的人，原来是蓝门咖啡馆的 Arthur。

lines.en: Emma tells me you need someone to fire questions at you in English. I might be able to help.
lines.zh: Emma 说你需要有人用英语连珠炮似的问你问题。我也许能帮上忙。

lines.en: Really? I thought you'd always run the café.
lines.zh: 真的？我还以为你一直在开咖啡馆。

lines.en: Only for the last twelve years. Before that, I taught English to adults for nearly thirty.
lines.zh: 只开了十二年。在那之前，我教了将近三十年的成人英语。

lines.en: You never mentioned it!
lines.zh: 你从来没提过！

lines.en: You never asked. Right, let's begin. Tell me about a place you like to visit.
lines.zh: 你也没问过。好，开始吧。说说一个你喜欢去的地方。

lines.en: Um, I like the canal. Because it's very nice. And, um, quiet.
lines.zh: 呃，我喜欢运河。因为它很好。而且，呃，安静。

lines.en: Stop there. What did you notice?
lines.zh: 停。你注意到什么了？

lines.en: I said 'um' too many times. And 'nice' doesn't really say anything.
lines.zh: 我说了太多“嗯”。而且 nice 这个词其实什么也没说。

lines.en: Exactly. Hesitating isn't the problem; everyone hesitates. The problem is that you stopped thinking in English and started translating.
lines.zh: 没错。犹豫不是问题，人人都会犹豫。问题是你不再用英语思考，开始翻译了。

lines.en: So what should I do instead?
lines.zh: 那我该怎么做？

lines.en: Buy yourself time with real phrases. 'That's an interesting question.' 'Let me think about that for a second.' Then paint me a picture.
lines.zh: 用地道的短语给自己争取时间：“这个问题很有意思。”“让我想一下。”然后给我描绘一幅画面。

lines.en: Let me think about that for a second. There's a stretch of the canal near here where the water is so still that the boats look as if they're floating on glass.
lines.zh: 让我想一下。这附近有一段运河，水面静得让那些船看起来像漂在玻璃上。

lines.en: Now that is a seven.
lines.zh: 这才是 7 分。

choice.q_zh: Arthur 教了你几句争取思考时间的话，你先试哪句？

lines.en: That's an interesting question.
lines.zh: 这是个很有意思的问题。

lines.en: Good. Now don't stop there. Keep going.
lines.zh: 好。别停，接着说。

lines.en: Could I try again with a different place?
lines.zh: 我能换个地方重新说吗？

lines.en: No. Same place, better words. Go on.
lines.zh: 不行。同一个地方，换更好的说法。来。

lines.en: My favourite student was a taxi driver called Bill. He was sixty-two.
lines.zh: 我最喜欢的学生是个出租车司机，叫 Bill，六十二岁。

lines.en: Why was he learning English? Wasn't he British?
lines.zh: 他为什么学英语？他不是英国人吗？

lines.en: He was learning to read. He'd hidden it for fifty years.
lines.zh: 他在学认字。他瞒了五十年。

lines.en: Every day, he read me one page of the newspaper. Just one. After a year, he read me a whole novel.
lines.zh: 他每天给我读一页报纸，就一页。一年后，他给我读完了一整本小说。

lines.en: One page a day. That's all it takes?
lines.zh: 一天一页。就这么简单？

lines.en: That, and refusing to stop. Fluency is a habit, not a talent.
lines.zh: 再加上不停下来。流利是习惯，不是天赋。

quiz.q: Arthur 开咖啡馆之前做什么？
Arthur 认为林真正的问题是什么？
options: 不再用英语思考，开始翻译

quiz.q: 他建议用什么争取思考时间？

episodes.next_zh: 第二天上班，一位难缠的客户把你的设计批得一无是处。

episodes.title: A Difficult Client
episodes.scene_zh: 公司让你负责一个新客户。第一次反馈会上，Hale 先生对设计一句好话都没有。

lines.en: I'll be honest with you. I don't like any of it. The colours are wrong, the logo's too small, and it doesn't feel premium.
lines.zh: 说实话，我一点都不喜欢。颜色不对，标志太小，而且没有高级感。

lines.en: I appreciate your honesty. Could you tell me a bit more about what 'premium' means to you?
lines.zh: 谢谢您直说。能多讲讲“高级感”对您来说是什么意思吗？

lines.en: You know. Expensive. Like a hotel lobby.
lines.zh: 你懂的。贵气。像酒店大堂那样。

lines.en: That's helpful. When we spoke last month, you said you wanted the brand to feel friendly and affordable. Has that changed?
lines.zh: 这很有帮助。上个月我们沟通时，您说希望品牌给人亲切、实惠的感觉。现在变了吗？

lines.en: Well, the board thinks we should aim a bit higher.
lines.zh: 嗯，董事会觉得我们应该定位再高一点。

lines.en: The deadline's on Friday, Lin. We can't start from scratch.
lines.zh: 周五就截止了，林。我们不可能从头再来。

lines.en: Mr Hale, may I suggest a compromise? We keep the overall layout, which tested very well, but we develop a darker, more elegant colour palette.
lines.zh: Hale 先生，我能提个折中方案吗？我们保留整体布局，它的测试效果很好；但配色改得更深、更优雅。

lines.en: And the logo?
lines.zh: 那标志呢？

lines.en: We can make it larger on the packaging, although I'd advise against changing it on the website, where space is limited.
lines.zh: 包装上可以放大，不过网站上我建议不要改，那里空间有限。

lines.en: Hmm. Can you show me something by Wednesday?
lines.zh: 嗯。周三之前能给我看点东西吗？

lines.en: We can have two options ready by Wednesday afternoon.
lines.zh: 周三下午我们可以准备好两个方案。

lines.en: Fine. Two options. Not ten.
lines.zh: 行。两个方案。别给我十个。

lines.en: That was masterful. You said no about four times and he didn't even notice.
lines.zh: 太高明了。你拒绝了他大概四次，他居然都没察觉。

choice.q_zh: 客户说董事会想“高端一点”，你追问：

lines.en: I see. Who on the board is pushing for this?
lines.zh: 明白了。董事会里是谁在推这件事？

lines.en: Mostly the new chairman. He likes gold. A lot of gold.
lines.zh: 主要是新来的董事长。他喜欢金色，非常喜欢。

lines.en: That's useful to know. Do you have any examples you like?
lines.zh: 这个信息很有用。您有喜欢的例子吗？

lines.en: I'll send you a few. They're all hotels, I'm afraid.
lines.zh: 我发几个给你。恐怕全是酒店。

lines.en: Teach me. How do you say no without saying no?
lines.zh: 教教我。你是怎么不说“不”却拒绝了的？

lines.en: First, thank them. Then ask a question. Then offer a smaller yes.
lines.zh: 先感谢，再提问，然后给一个小一点的“可以”。

lines.en: A smaller yes. I like that. Can I have a pay rise?
lines.zh: 小一点的“可以”。我喜欢。我能涨工资吗？

lines.en: Thank you for asking. What did you have in mind? Perhaps we could start with a biscuit.
lines.zh: 谢谢你问。你想要多少？也许我们可以先从一块饼干开始。

lines.en: That was brutal. Brilliant, but brutal.
lines.zh: 太狠了。漂亮，但是狠。

quiz.q: Hale 先生现在想要什么感觉？
林提出的折中方案是？
options: 保留布局，配色改得更深更优雅

quiz.q: Tom 说林最厉害的地方是？
options: 拒绝了好几次对方却没察觉

episodes.next_zh: 方案过了。可周四的部门会上，你得用一张图表说清楚这个项目带来了什么。

episodes.title: The Numbers
episodes.scene_zh: 部门会议上，你要用一张图表说明新设计带来了什么变化。

lines.en: Two minutes until the meeting. Have you got your figures ready?
lines.zh: 还有两分钟开会。数据准备好了吗？

lines.en: Yes, but I'm worried I'll just read out numbers and send everyone to sleep.
lines.zh: 好了，但我怕自己只是念数字，把大家念睡着。

lines.en: Then don't. Tell them what the numbers mean.
lines.zh: 那就别念。告诉他们这些数字意味着什么。

lines.en: Good morning, everyone. This chart shows visits to the client's website over the past twelve months.
lines.zh: 大家早上好。这张图显示的是过去十二个月客户网站的访问量。

lines.en: As you can see, traffic remained fairly stable until June, and then rose sharply after the new design was launched.
lines.zh: 可以看到，访问量到六月一直比较平稳，新设计上线后急剧上升。

lines.en: It peaked in August at just over forty thousand visits, roughly double the figure for January.
lines.zh: 八月达到峰值，略超过四万次，大约是一月的两倍。

lines.en: Was that increase sustained, or was it just a summer effect?
lines.zh: 这个增长持续下去了吗，还是只是夏天的效应？

lines.en: Good question. Visits fell slightly in September, but they've levelled off at a much higher level than before.
lines.zh: 好问题。九月略有下降，但之后稳定在了比以前高得多的水平。

lines.en: Overall, the redesign appears to have had a significant and lasting impact.
lines.zh: 总的来说，这次改版似乎带来了显著而持久的影响。

lines.en: And what about sales?
lines.zh: 那销售额呢？

lines.en: Online sales followed a similar pattern, although the increase was more gradual.
lines.zh: 线上销售额的趋势相似，不过增长更平缓一些。

lines.en: You see? Nobody fell asleep. Even the finance director asked a question.
lines.zh: 看到没？没人睡着。连财务总监都提问了。

lines.en: He asked where the biscuits were.
lines.zh: 他问的是饼干在哪儿。

choice.q_zh: Tom 让你讲数字背后的意思，你问：

lines.en: So I should start with the conclusion?
lines.zh: 所以我应该先说结论？

lines.en: Exactly. Headline first, then the details.
lines.zh: 没错。先说标题，再讲细节。

lines.en: Should I make a joke at the start?
lines.zh: 开头要不要讲个笑话？

lines.en: Only if it's better than mine. So, no.
lines.zh: 除非比我讲得好。所以，不要。

lines.en: Can you check my list? Rise, increase, climb, peak.
lines.zh: 帮我看看这个表？上升、增加、攀升、达到顶点。

lines.en: Good. And going down?
lines.zh: 不错。那下降呢？

lines.en: Fall, drop, decline, dip. And when nothing changes, it levels off or remains stable.
lines.zh: 下跌、下降、减少、小幅下滑。不变的时候就是趋于平稳、保持稳定。

lines.en: And when it goes up very fast?
lines.zh: 那涨得特别快呢？

lines.en: It soars. Like my confidence, right now.
lines.zh: 飙升。就像我现在的自信。

quiz.q: 网站访问量什么时候开始急剧上升？
八月的访问量大约是一月的多少？
“levelled off” 是什么意思？

episodes.next_zh: 考试前一晚，你几乎没睡。第二天一早，Emma 坚持要送你去考场。

episodes.title: Test Day
episodes.scene_zh: 考试当天。上午笔试，下午口语。

lines.en: Have you got your passport? Pencils? Water?
lines.zh: 护照带了吗？铅笔？水？

lines.en: Yes, yes and yes. Emma, you're more nervous than I am.
lines.zh: 带了，带了，带了。Emma，你比我还紧张。

lines.en: Somebody has to be. Go on. You've got this.
lines.zh: 总得有人紧张吧。去吧，你没问题的。

lines.en: Good afternoon. In this part of the test, I'm going to give you a topic, and I'd like you to talk about it for one to two minutes.
lines.zh: 下午好。这一部分我会给你一个话题，请你讲一到两分钟。

lines.en: Describe a time when you helped someone. You should say who you helped, how you helped them, and explain how you felt about it.
lines.zh: 描述一次你帮助别人的经历。你应该说明帮了谁、怎么帮的，并解释你的感受。

lines.en: I'd like to talk about something that happened last summer, when I was working in Edinburgh.
lines.zh: 我想讲去年夏天在爱丁堡工作时发生的一件事。

lines.en: A friend of mine was running a small dinner club, and on the night of an important event, a storm flooded the street outside.
lines.zh: 我的一个朋友在经营一家小餐会，在一场重要活动的当晚，暴雨淹了外面的街道。

lines.en: Most people would probably have cancelled, but we decided to move everything to a hall nearby and carry the food through the rain.
lines.zh: 大多数人可能会取消，但我们决定把所有东西搬到附近的大厅，冒雨把菜端过去。

lines.en: What I learned from it is that helping someone isn't always about solving their problem. Sometimes it's simply about refusing to let them face it alone.
lines.zh: 我从中学到的是，帮助别人不一定是替他解决问题。有时只是不让他独自面对。

lines.en: Thank you. Do you think people are less willing to help strangers than they used to be?
lines.zh: 谢谢。你认为现在的人比过去更不愿意帮助陌生人吗？

lines.en: That's a difficult question. I suspect it depends less on the era than on the environment.
lines.zh: 这个问题挺难的。我觉得这更多取决于环境，而不是时代。

lines.en: In big cities, people can seem indifferent, but in my experience that's often shyness rather than a lack of kindness.
lines.zh: 在大城市里，人们看起来可能很冷漠，但据我的经验，那往往是害羞，而不是缺少善意。

lines.en: Thank you. That's the end of the speaking test.
lines.zh: 谢谢。口语考试到此结束。

choice.q_zh: 进考场前，你对 Emma 说：

lines.en: Thanks, Emma. I'll call you as soon as I'm out.
lines.zh: 谢谢你，Emma。我一出来就给你打电话。

lines.en: I'll be at Arthur's, eating far too many scones.
lines.zh: 我会在 Arthur 那儿，吃太多司康饼。

lines.en: If I fail, I'm blaming your coffee.
lines.zh: 要是没考好，我就怪你的咖啡。

lines.en: Fine. And if you pass, I'm taking all the credit.
lines.zh: 行。那要是考过了，功劳全是我的。

lines.en: Let's talk about your hometown. Where is it, and what is it like?
lines.zh: 聊聊你的家乡吧。在哪儿，是什么样的？

lines.en: I'm from Hangzhou, a city in eastern China that's famous for its lake and its green tea.
lines.zh: 我来自杭州，中国东部的一座城市，以西湖和绿茶闻名。

lines.en: Would you like to live there again in the future?
lines.zh: 你将来还想回去住吗？

lines.en: Possibly. It's a wonderful place to grow old, but at the moment I'm enjoying being somewhere that challenges me.
lines.zh: 也许吧。那是个养老的好地方，不过现在我更享受待在一个能挑战我的地方。

lines.en: Thank you. Now I'd like to move on to Part Two.
lines.zh: 谢谢。现在我们进入第二部分。

quiz.q: 口语第二部分的题目是？
options: 描述一个你喜欢的地方
描述一次你帮助别人的经历

quiz.q: 林讲的是哪件事？
options: 帮 Hale 先生改设计

quiz.q: 林认为大城市的人看起来冷漠，往往是因为？

episodes.next_zh: 两周后的一个早上，成绩邮件来了。你不敢点开。

episodes.title: The Results
episodes.scene_zh: 考试两周后，成绩出来了。你把手机递给了 Emma。

lines.en: It's here. The email has arrived. I can't open it.
lines.zh: 来了。邮件到了。我不敢打开。

lines.en: Give me your phone. Right. Are you ready?
lines.zh: 手机给我。好了，准备好了吗？

lines.en: No. Yes. Just read it.
lines.zh: 没有。好了。你就念吧。

lines.en: Listening, seven and a half. Reading, seven.
lines.zh: 听力 7.5，阅读 7。

lines.en: And writing? Writing was the one I was worried about.
lines.zh: 写作呢？我最担心的就是写作。

lines.en: Writing, six and a half.
Six and a half. That's not enough, is it?
Hang on. Speaking, seven and a half. Overall... seven! Lin, it's a seven!
lines.zh: 等等。口语 7.5。总分……7！林，是 7 分！

lines.en: But they said no section below six and a half. Let me check. Yes, six and a half is the minimum. I've actually done it.
lines.zh: 可他们说单项不能低于 6.5。我查一下……对，6.5 是最低要求。我真的做到了。

lines.en: Of course you have. Right, I'm calling Tom, and we're all going to Arthur's.
lines.zh: 你当然做到了。好，我给 Tom 打电话，我们都去 Arthur 那儿。

lines.en: Seven and a half in speaking? I'll have you know I take full credit for that.
lines.zh: 口语 7.5？告诉你，这份功劳全归我。

lines.en: You can take half the credit. The other half goes to the canal and its floating boats.
lines.zh: 你可以拿一半功劳。另一半归那条运河，还有它上面漂着的船。

lines.en: Oh no. Read the rest quickly, before I faint.
lines.zh: 完了。快把剩下的读完，我要晕了。

lines.en: Breathe, Lin. Just breathe. There's more.
lines.zh: 呼吸，林，深呼吸。还没完呢。

lines.en: I knew it. My essays were always too long.
lines.zh: 我就知道，我的作文总是写太长。

lines.en: Too long is better than too short. Hang on, there's more.
lines.zh: 长总比短好。等等，还有。

lines.en: Everyone, raise your cups. Tea, coffee, whatever you've got.
lines.zh: 大家举杯。茶、咖啡，手里有什么举什么。

lines.en: To Lin, who arrived with a key that didn't work and a lot of courage that did.
lines.zh: 敬林：她来的时候钥匙不管用，可勇气一直管用。

lines.en: To Lin!
lines.zh: 敬林！

lines.en: And to Arthur, who never told me he was a teacher. Thank you for every question.
lines.zh: 也敬 Arthur，他从没告诉我他是老师。谢谢您问的每一个问题。

lines.en: The pleasure was mine. Now, who wants a scone?
lines.zh: 我的荣幸。好了，谁要司康饼？

quiz.q: 林的总分是多少？
哪一项分数最低？
学校要求单项不低于多少？

episodes.next_zh: 分数够了，还有最后一关：和教授面谈。

episodes.title: The Interview
episodes.scene_zh: 你走进大学设计学院的办公室。Reed 博士正在翻看你的作品集。

lines.en: Thank you for coming in, Lin. I've had a look at your portfolio. The Edinburgh posters are particularly striking.
lines.zh: 谢谢你过来，林。我看了你的作品集，爱丁堡的那些海报尤其令人印象深刻。

lines.en: Thank you. To be honest, they were designed in a bit of a hurry, but I think the pressure actually helped.
lines.zh: 谢谢。说实话，那些是赶出来的，但我觉得压力反而有帮助。

lines.en: Let's talk about why you want to do this course. You already have a good job. What's missing?
lines.zh: 说说你为什么想读这个课程吧。你已经有一份不错的工作了。缺了什么？

lines.en: I'd say my job has taught me how to solve problems, but not always how to ask the right questions in the first place.
lines.zh: 我想说，工作教会了我怎么解决问题，但不总是教我一开始该问什么问题。

lines.en: Go on.
lines.zh: 继续说。

lines.en: For instance, when a client asks for something to feel 'premium', I can deliver that. But I'd like to understand why some designs make people feel welcome, while others make them feel excluded.
lines.zh: 比如，客户要“高级感”，我能做出来。但我想弄明白，为什么有些设计让人觉得被欢迎，有些却让人觉得被排斥。

lines.en: That's essentially a question about public space, which is exactly what our second term focuses on.
lines.zh: 这本质上是关于公共空间的问题，正是我们第二学期的重点。

lines.en: That's precisely why I applied to this programme rather than any other.
lines.zh: 这正是我申请这个项目而不是别的项目的原因。

lines.en: One more question. Part-time study on top of a full-time job is exhausting. How will you manage?
lines.zh: 最后一个问题。全职工作之外再在职读书会非常累。你打算怎么应对？

lines.en: I won't pretend it'll be easy. But I've just spent a year learning a language in my spare time, so I have a fairly realistic idea of what it takes.
lines.zh: 我不会假装这很容易。但我刚用业余时间学了一年语言，所以我对需要付出什么心里有数。

lines.en: Fair point. You'll hear from us within a week.
lines.zh: 有道理。一周内我们会通知你。

choice.q_zh: Reed 博士夸了你的海报，你接着说：

lines.en: Would you like me to talk you through the process?
lines.zh: 需要我讲讲设计过程吗？

lines.en: Briefly, yes. I'm always more curious about process than results.
lines.zh: 简单讲讲吧。比起结果，我一向更好奇过程。

lines.en: Is there anything in particular you'd like to know about them?
lines.zh: 关于这些海报，您有什么特别想了解的吗？

lines.en: Mostly why you chose such a quiet colour for such a noisy festival.
lines.zh: 主要是，为什么给那么吵的艺术节选了这么安静的颜色。

lines.en: Lin, one more thing, off the record.
lines.zh: 林，还有一件事，私下说。

lines.en: Of course.
lines.zh: 您请说。

lines.en: Most applicants tell me what they know. You told me what you don't know. That's rarer than you think.
lines.zh: 大多数申请人跟我说他们懂什么，你跟我说你不懂什么。这比你想的少见。

lines.en: I've had a lot of practice not knowing things this year.
lines.zh: 这一年我可没少练习“不懂”。

lines.en: Keep practising. It's the best qualification there is.
lines.zh: 继续练。这是最好的资历。

quiz.q: Reed 博士对哪些作品印象最深？
林说工作没能教会她什么？
林为什么觉得自己能应付在职学习？
options: 刚用业余时间学了一年语言

episodes.next_zh: 一周后，录取通知来了。一月，你第一次走进研讨课的教室。

episodes.title: The Seminar
episodes.scene_zh: 一月，第一次研讨课。同学 Priya 观点鲜明，Reed 博士喜欢让大家争论。

lines.en: This week's question: should public spaces be designed to discourage certain kinds of behaviour? Priya, would you like to start?
lines.zh: 本周的问题：公共空间是否应该通过设计来阻止某些行为？Priya，你先来？

lines.en: I think they have to be, to some extent. Nobody wants a park where people feel unsafe at night.
lines.zh: 我觉得在一定程度上必须这样。没人想要一个晚上让人觉得不安全的公园。

lines.en: I take your point, but I'd question who gets to decide what counts as unsafe.
lines.zh: 我明白你的意思，但我想问：谁来决定什么算“不安全”？

lines.en: Meaning what, exactly?
lines.zh: 具体是什么意思？

lines.en: Well, benches with a bar in the middle are often presented as a safety measure, but in practice they mainly stop homeless people from lying down.
lines.zh: 比如，中间加一根横杆的长椅常被说成是安全措施，但实际上主要是为了不让无家可归的人躺下。

lines.en: That's true, although I'm not convinced the designers always intend that.
lines.zh: 确实，不过我不确定设计师总是有意这样做。

lines.en: Possibly not. But if the effect is consistently the same, the intention becomes rather less relevant.
lines.zh: 也许不是。但如果效果始终如一，那么初衷就没那么重要了。

lines.en: Interesting. Priya, is there a way to design for safety without excluding anyone?
lines.zh: 有意思。Priya，有没有办法既保证安全又不排斥任何人？

lines.en: Better lighting, perhaps. More reasons for people to be around in the evening. Things that make everyone feel safer, rather than pushing some people out.
lines.zh: 也许是更好的照明，让人们晚上有更多理由在那儿。让每个人都觉得更安全，而不是把一部分人赶走。

lines.en: I'd agree with that entirely. It's the difference between designing against people and designing for them.
lines.zh: 这一点我完全同意。这就是“针对人的设计”和“为人的设计”的区别。

lines.en: Excellent. That's your essay title for next week, by the way.
lines.zh: 很好。顺便说一句，这就是你们下周的论文题目。

lines.en: Thanks a lot, Lin.
lines.zh: 真是谢谢你了，林。

lines.en: But I'm happy to be proved wrong if you have an example.
lines.zh: 不过你要是能举出例子，我很乐意被说服。

lines.en: I might. Give me a week and a library card.
lines.zh: 也许有。给我一个星期和一张借书证。

lines.en: Sorry, I didn't mean to sound so certain.
lines.zh: 抱歉，我不是想说得这么绝对。

lines.en: Don't apologise. Disagreeing is the fun part.
lines.zh: 别道歉。争论才是好玩的部分。

lines.en: For the record, I agreed with you more than I admitted.
lines.zh: 说句实话，我其实比嘴上承认的更同意你。

lines.en: Then why did you argue so hard?
lines.zh: 那你为什么争得那么凶？

lines.en: Someone has to play devil's advocate. Otherwise, the seminar is just people nodding.
lines.zh: 总得有人唱反调。不然研讨课就只剩大家点头了。

lines.en: "Devil's advocate." I'm adding that to my notebook.
lines.zh: “唱反调”。我要把它记进笔记本。

lines.en: Same time next week? I'll bring better arguments.
lines.zh: 下周同一时间？我会带更好的论据来。

quiz.q: 这次研讨课讨论的问题是？
options: 公共空间该不该用设计阻止某些行为

quiz.q: 林认为中间加横杆的长椅实际上是为了？
options: 不让无家可归的人躺下

quiz.q: Priya 最后的 “Thanks a lot, Lin.” 是什么语气？
options: 开玩笑地抱怨（害她多了论文要写）

episodes.next_zh: 就在这时，Jake 又打来了电话：一年之约快到了。

episodes.title: The Offer Stands
episodes.scene_zh: 深夜，你的手机响了。是 Jake，从纽约打来。

lines.en: Lin! It's been almost a year. I said the offer stands, and I meant it. New York wants you.
lines.zh: 林！快一年了。我说过邀请一直有效，我是认真的。纽约需要你。

lines.en: Jake, it's lovely to hear from you. And I'm genuinely flattered.
lines.zh: Jake，真高兴接到你的电话。我真的受宠若惊。

lines.en: I can hear a 'but' coming.
lines.zh: 我听出来后面要说“但是”了。

lines.en: There is a 'but'. I've just started my master's, and I'm not going to walk away from it.
lines.zh: 确实有个“但是”。我刚开始读硕士，不会半途放弃。

lines.en: OK. So what would it take?
lines.zh: 好吧。那要怎样你才愿意？

lines.en: What if, instead of a full-time job, we talked about a single project over the summer, when the course takes a break?
lines.zh: 如果不是全职工作，而是暑假课程休息时做一个项目，怎么样？

lines.en: Three months? I'd need you for at least four.
lines.zh: 三个月？我至少需要你四个月。

lines.en: Could we meet in the middle? Three months in New York, and I'll do the early concept work remotely from London.
lines.zh: 我们各让一步？在纽约待三个月，前期的概念设计我在伦敦远程做。

lines.en: You've turned into a tough negotiator, you know that?
lines.zh: 你变成一个难对付的谈判高手了，知道吗？

lines.en: I've had a lot of practice lately. Mostly with a client who wanted everything to look like a hotel lobby.
lines.zh: 最近练得多。主要是跟一个什么都想做成酒店大堂的客户。

lines.en: All right, deal. Three months, plus the remote work. I'll send you the details.
lines.zh: 好，成交。三个月，加上远程的部分。我把细节发给你。

lines.en: Thank you, Jake. Honestly, this is the best of both worlds.
lines.zh: 谢谢你，Jake。说真的，这是两全其美。

choice.q_zh: Jake 问你要什么条件，你先说：

lines.en: Give me a second to think about that.
lines.zh: 让我想一下。

lines.en: Take two. I'll wait. I'm a very patient man.
lines.zh: 想两下也行。我等着，我很有耐心。

lines.en: Honestly? A small miracle. But let's try.
lines.zh: 说实话？要一个小奇迹。不过可以试试。

lines.en: I've produced miracles before. Mostly cheap ones.
lines.zh: 奇迹我又不是没制作过。大多是便宜的那种。

lines.en: Lin? It's half past twelve. Is everything all right?
lines.zh: 林？十二点半了，没事吧？

lines.en: Everything's perfect. I'm going to New York. Just for the summer.
lines.zh: 一切都好。我要去纽约了，就一个夏天。

lines.en: You said no to Jake twice, and now you're going anyway?
lines.zh: 你拒绝了 Jake 两次，结果还是要去？

lines.en: I didn't say yes to his offer. I made him say yes to mine.
lines.zh: 我不是答应了他的条件，是让他答应了我的。

lines.en: That's the most Lin thing you've ever said. Now go to sleep.
lines.zh: 这是你说过的最像你的一句话。快睡吧。

quiz.q: 林为什么不接受全职工作？
options: 刚开始读硕士，不想放弃

quiz.q: 最后谈成了什么？
options: 暑假去纽约三个月，前期在伦敦远程做

quiz.q: “the best of both worlds” 是什么意思？

episodes.next_zh: 出发去纽约前，蓝门咖啡馆要办一场特别的分享会——主讲人是你。

episodes.title: Full Circle
episodes.scene_zh: 去纽约之前，Arthur 在蓝门咖啡馆为你办了一场小小的分享会。

lines.en: Ladies and gentlemen, a year and a half ago, someone knocked on my door in the pouring rain. Tonight, they're going to tell you what happened next.
lines.zh: 女士们先生们，一年半以前，有人在倾盆大雨里敲了我的门。今晚，由这位来讲讲后来发生的事。

lines.en: Thank you, Arthur. When I first arrived in London, I couldn't even open my own front door. The key was wrong, and so, I thought, was my English.
lines.zh: 谢谢你，Arthur。我刚到伦敦的时候，连自己家的门都打不开。钥匙是错的，我当时觉得，我的英语也是错的。

lines.en: What I've come to realise is that learning a language isn't really about being correct. It's about being brave enough to be understood.
lines.zh: 后来我慢慢明白，学语言其实不是为了永远正确，而是要有勇气让别人听懂你。

lines.en: I made mistakes in shops, at work, in front of investors and once, memorably, in front of an entire theatre.
lines.zh: 我在商店里犯过错，在公司犯过错，在投资人面前犯过错，还有一次——令人难忘地——在整个剧院的人面前。

lines.en: But every single one of those mistakes led me to a person. A neighbour, a colleague, a friend.
lines.zh: 但每一个错误都把我带到了一个人身边。一个邻居，一个同事，一个朋友。

lines.en: And a very patient flatmate!
lines.zh: 还有一个超有耐心的室友！

lines.en: Yes, her too. So if any of you are learning something difficult right now, my advice is simple.
lines.zh: 对，还有她。所以，如果你们中有人正在学一样很难的东西，我的建议很简单。

lines.en: Do a little every day. Talk to people, even when it's frightening. And don't wait until you feel ready, because nobody ever does.
lines.zh: 每天做一点。和人说话，哪怕会害怕。别等到觉得自己准备好了，因为没有人会真的准备好。

lines.en: Speech! Oh, wait. That was the speech.
lines.zh: 来一段演讲！哦，等等，刚才那就是演讲。

lines.en: There's one more thing. Sophie sent this down from Edinburgh. She said you'd know what to do with it.
lines.zh: 还有一件事。Sophie 从爱丁堡寄来了这个，她说你知道该怎么做。

lines.en: A notebook, with a note inside: 'For the next person, who needs it more than I do.'
lines.zh: 一本笔记本，里面夹着一张纸条：“给下一个比我更需要它的人。”

lines.en: So who's the next person?
lines.zh: 那下一个人是谁？

lines.en: I have a feeling I'll find out in New York.
lines.zh: 我有种感觉，到了纽约我就会知道。

choice.q_zh: 说到每个错误都让你认识了一个人，你点名感谢：

lines.en: Arthur, who taught me to paint pictures with words.
lines.zh: Arthur，他教我用话语画画。

lines.en: Tom, who taught me that "not bad" means "really good".
lines.zh: Tom，他教我“还不赖”的意思是“真的很好”。

options.label_zh: 感谢 Patel 太太和 Sophie

lines.en: Mrs Patel, who sold me milk and gave me advice for free.
lines.zh: Patel 太太，她卖给我牛奶，还免费送我建议。

lines.en: Sophie, whom I'd never met, but who left me a map.
lines.zh: Sophie，我当时从没见过她，她却给我留了一张地图。

lines.en: Before you go, take this. It's the last tin of Rose's blue paint.
lines.zh: 走之前拿着这个。这是 Rose 留下的最后一罐蓝漆。

lines.en: Arthur, I can't take this. It's from your door.
lines.zh: Arthur，我不能收。这是您门上的颜色。

lines.en: The door has had forty years of luck. It's time the blue travelled.
lines.zh: 这扇门已经走了四十年运，该让这抹蓝去旅行了。

lines.en: Then I'll find a door in New York that needs it.
lines.zh: 那我就在纽约找一扇需要它的门。

lines.en: Rose would have liked you. Safe travels, my dear.
lines.zh: Rose 一定会喜欢你。一路平安，孩子。

quiz.q: 林刚到伦敦时遇到了什么事？
林认为学语言的关键是什么？
Sophie 托 Arthur 交给林的是？

episodes.next_zh: 第三季完。第四季：纽约——那本笔记本，要交给下一个人。
